work.title: A few systems I've designed and built end to end.

lery.title: Lery AI
lery.summary: A screen-less, voice-first English tutor that runs on a Raspberry Pi.
lery.problem: Many learners freeze when they have to speak. A naive LLM tutor makes it worse: give it a long prompt and it answers an A1 student at B2 level. Lery treats the model as one component in a system that controls what it sees, when, and how its output is checked.
lery.role: Design and development across the device voice loop, agent service, API and mobile app.
highlights: Layered context with explicit token budgets, plus just-in-time retrieval through tool calls instead of injecting full history every turn.
Compliance gate for beginner levels: typed violations are fed back to the tutor for one corrective retry before anything is spoken.
Every turn scored on four CEFR pillars using schema-constrained output, with eval fixtures and a synthetic student to test the pipeline.
OpenTelemetry traces showed two independent LLM checks running in series; running them in parallel removed a full call from the critical path.
gallery: Lery AI cover: “The English tutor that talks back”, with the mascot and cards showing a Portuguese sentence, the bridge-mode level, the English reply, a score of 92 and the share of English spoken.

Lery AI architecture overview, “Under the hood of Lery”: the Raspberry Pi device (wake word, Whisper, bridge mode, Gemini, Edge TTS, LED and mascot), the multi-agent brain, the Fastify and Prisma API with PostgreSQL, a React dashboard and an Expo app, plus the research it rests on and project numbers.

boua.title: Boua
boua.summary: A social app for finding and hosting nights out — from a house party to a paid event.
boua.problem: Knowing where the good night is usually means scrolling a dozen Instagram stories. Boua puts what's happening nearby on one feed and map, and lets anyone host — free or with paid entry — from the same app and the same account.
boua.role: Product, design and full stack development — mobile app, API, web and landing page.
highlights: pnpm monorepo: an Expo app, a Fastify API and web apps sharing typed API contracts and design tokens through internal packages.
Payments sit behind a provider interface, so Stripe or a local stub is picked by configuration; idempotency keys keep retries from charging twice.
QR tickets are RS256-signed for tamper evidence, but validation always re-checks the code against the database — the signature is never the source of truth.
Pulse: live crowd ratings in rounds during an event — vibe, sound, crowd, queue.
gallery: Boua landing page: “Before you leave the house, see how the night is going”, with phones showing a live Pulse score, the map and the home feed.
Three Boua app screens: the home deck of nights out, the live map of the city and an event page with confirmed guests and a host notice.
Three Boua app screens: a live Pulse vote with an emoji dial, the night's “Espiada” photo stories and the My nights list.
Three Boua app screens: the new-night sheet, the create-a-night form and a night hosted by a friend.

colete.title: Colete
colete.summary: A mobile-first web app for organizing weekly pickup football games.
colete.problem: Attendance, team draws, live scores, stats, rankings and awards usually live in a group chat and someone's memory. Colete puts the whole game night in one place, and makes the results shareable.
colete.role: Product, design and full stack development.
highlights: Statistics are derived from game events — goals, assists, awards — so there are no redundant counters to drift out of sync.
Authorization checked per group on every server action; private groups return 404 so their existence isn't revealed.
Invites use random tokens with revocation, expiry and usage limits.
Dynamic Open Graph images for public games, rankings and player cards.
gallery: Colete landing page: headline, sign-in with Google and phones showing the live game screen.
Colete player profile in dark mode with rating, achievements, all-time stats and a shareable player card. Demo data.
Three Colete app screens from the landing page: a live game with the score and plays, the home with the next game and lineup, and the season ranking. Demo data.

nexustrace.title: NexusTrace
nexustrace.summary: Fraud detection over a graph of financial transactions.
nexustrace.problem: Fraud rings hide in relationships, not in single transactions. NexusTrace loads accounts and transfers into Neo4j, groups them into communities and scores every account by how money actually moves through the network.
nexustrace.role: Built as a team integrator project at UNISAL; I maintain the public repository.
highlights: Louvain community detection with Neo4j Graph Data Science, run on startup over synthetic account and transaction data.
Explainable risk scores from fan-in, volume z-score and cross-community behaviour, with configurable rules.
FastAPI service pushing anomaly events over WebSockets to a Next.js dashboard with an interactive force graph.
An AI analyst on GPT-4.1 that answers questions by calling the same risk API through tool calling.
gallery: NexusTrace cover: “Fraud hides in the connections”, with a graph of account communities, a high-risk account receiving transfers from 17 accounts, risk signals and a note from the AI analyst. Synthetic data.

aresta.title: Aresta Studio
aresta.summary: The website for my independent software studio, designed and built end to end.
aresta.problem: A studio site has one job: make a business owner trust you enough to describe their problem. Aresta leads with problems instead of a list of services, shows real cases and turns the first contact into a structured brief.
highlights: Brief form as a Server Action with field validation, a honeypot and transactional emails built with React Email.
Isometric illustration system drawn in code, with light and dark themes and entrance motion that steps aside under reduced motion.
Dynamic Open Graph images and a route that renders Instagram carousels from the same components as the site.
gallery: Aresta Studio home page in dark mode: headline about turning complex ideas into real products, with an isometric illustration.
Problems section of the Aresta site: isometric illustrations next to common business pains and how they are solved.
Process section of the Aresta site, from understanding the problem to production, in light mode.

about.title: I like software that holds up after the demo.
paragraphs: I'm a full stack developer from Potim, Brazil, with 3+ years building systems people rely on every day — first a CRM, help desk, intranet and digital signatures at Editora Santuário, and now academic and administrative platforms at UNISAL, where I own the work from solution design to deploy.

I care about the parts users never see: clear domain boundaries, authorization that holds up, performance I've actually measured, and tests where they matter. With AI, my focus is the engineering around the model — context, tool calling, structured output, evals and observability. I build, measure, and only then optimize.

faq.title: Quick answers about who I am and what I do.

items.a: Talles Amaral is a Full Stack Developer from Potim, Brazil. Since April 2025 he works at UNISAL, where he designs, builds and evolves the university's internal systems, and on his own time he builds products such as Lery, Boua, Colete and Aresta Studio.

items.q: Which technologies does he work with?
items.a: TypeScript, React, Next.js, React Native and Expo on the front end; Node.js (Fastify, NestJS), .NET Core and Python (FastAPI) on the back end; PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL and Neo4j for data; Docker, CI/CD and AWS for delivery.

items.q: Does he work with AI and LLMs?
items.a: Yes. His AI work is about the engineering around the model: context engineering, tool calling, structured output, evals and observability. Lery, his Computer Engineering thesis, is a voice-first English tutor built this way, and NexusTrace pairs a graph-based risk engine with an AI analyst.

At UNISAL: SIGA, a real-time queue system, and a Social Service platform serving 678 students. Personally: Lery AI (voice-first English tutor), Boua (social app for nights out), Colete (app for organizing weekly football games) and Aresta Studio (his software studio's website). With a team: NexusTrace, fraud detection with graph analytics.

items.q: How much experience does he have?
items.a: Three-plus years in production. He was a Junior Developer at Editora Santuário from December 2022 to April 2025 (CRM, LGPD-compliant digital signatures, help desk and an intranet integrated with TOTVS RM) and has been a Full Stack Developer at UNISAL since April 2025.

items.q: Where did he study and which languages does he speak?
items.a: He is pursuing a Bachelor's in Computer Engineering at UNISAL (since January 2022). He speaks Portuguese (native) and English (B1/B2).
By email at contact@tallesamaral.dev. He is also on LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/tallesamaral) and GitHub (github.com/tlsamaral).
